controls: Keep the scalar NONE-base decode_vector untouched so non-RVV and fallback builds produce the original bit pattern
Gate the new override with the same #ifdef COMPILE_SIMD_RISCV_RVV used by existing sq-rvv.cpp kernels
Add a unit-style comparison harness that decodes random codes through RVV and scalar paths and reports max abs/rel diff, and treat any nibble-order bug as a hard failure
Never assume a fixed VLEN or a d multiple of VLEN; derive vl from remaining count each iteration
reasons: Replacing the exact /15.0f with a reciprocal multiply changes the last-bit FP rounding of reconstructed components, which can propagate into downstream distance values
Interleaving low/high nibbles back into component order is the classic even/odd lane-ordering bug site
A VLEN-agnostic tail is mandatory; an off-by-one on packed byte loads can read past code_size
A new duplicate decode path increases maintenance surface across NONE/AVX2/AVX512/RVV variants

conditions.description: The library is built with COMPILE_SIMD_RISCV_RVV (metadata shows rv64* v1p0/zvl128b build ISA)
Runtime SIMD dispatch in sq-dispatch.h selects SIMDLevel::RISCV_RVV for QT_4bit so the RVV tag-quantizer is reached
d can be any value including odd; tail must be handled VLEN-agnostically

actions.proposal: Add a real VLEN-agnostic RVV decode_vector override to the QuantizerTemplate RISCV_RVV specializations in faiss/impl/scalar_quantizer/sq-rvv.cpp (NON_UNIFORM, and UNIFORM for consistency), mirroring the AVX2/AVX512 Codec4bit decode_8/16_components approach without any fixed width: strip-mined loop that loads vl/2 packed code bytes (vle8), unpacks low/high 4-bit nibbles (vand 0x0F / vsrl 4 or even-odd deinterleave), converts to float (vzext + vfwcvt.f.xu or vwf), applies the affine decode (0.5f*inv15 offset and inv15 scale via precomputed scalars), and fuses vmin[i]+vdiff[i]*x with vfmacc against contiguous vmin/vdiff vectors, ending with vse32 for the even/odd interleaved component order; keep fixed-VL main loop plus runtime-VL tail per kernel conventions and leave the scalar NONE base as the fallback for non-RVV builds.

correctness_checks: Run faiss sq-decode benchmark/known-answer check comparing reconstructed vectors RVV vs scalar NONE base for QT_4bit and QT_4bit_uniform
Cover d in {1, VL-1, VL, VL+1, odd, 2*VL} and empty input; verify no out-of-bounds nibble load on the last byte
Confirm the even/odd nibble-to-component ordering matches Codec4bit<NONE>::decode_component on exhaustive nibble patterns 0..15

controls: Document the exact rounding delta of reciprocal multiply vs divide before shipping and gate on the project's tolerance policy
Keep a bit-exact /15.0f variant behind a flag if any downstream path requires it
Verify with a micro-benchmark that hoisting the reciprocal does not pessimize the OoO overlap of independent iterations
reasons: reciprocal multiply is not bit-exact with /15.0f (rounding, subnormal handling)
changing the scalar fallback's arithmetic could change reconstruction for non-RVV platforms
index strength reduction in the scalar path is a micro-optimization whose benefit depends on the actual pipeline

conditions.description: Only fold the constant division where the project permits the (nibble*inv15 + 0.5f*inv15) form; otherwise keep /15.0f in any retained scalar fallback
A precomputed reciprocal inv15 = 1.0f/15.0f must be loaded once per call/vector, not per element

actions.proposal: Eliminate the per-component true division and hoist loop overhead: precompute inv15 = 1.0f/15.0f once and express the decode as nibble*inv15 + (0.5f*inv15), then fold into vmin[i] + vdiff[i]*x with a single fused multiply-accumulate; in the RVV path this becomes vector-scalar vfmul + vfadd + vfmacc with no vfdiv in the body; if the scalar fallback must remain for non-RVV builds, make the same algebraic replacement only where the project accepts the rounding change and also replace the i/2, (i&1)<<2 index recomputation with a step-pointer increment.

gaps.description: Hardware ISA and runtime VLEN are not directly recorded: metadata gives the build ISA (rv64*_v1p0_..._zvl128b) but not the /proc/cpuinfo 'isa' line or vlenb CSR, so hardware V presence and VLEN (>=128 implied by zvl128b) are inferred, not confirmed.

perf stat cpu_cycle and instruction counters hold 2^63 sentinel/saturated values, so the IPC=1 figure and any cycles/element baseline are unreliable; bound-type evidence rests on duration and cache/branch rates only.

Only 3 cpu-clock samples were captured for the target function, all attributed to the final fsw; sampling-IP precision is unknown, so per-instruction attribution beyond the loop interval is not supported.

No per-element cycle budget or A/B speedup measurement exists for decode_vector; benchmark_QT_4bit_cpu_time_ns (1,280,779 ns) is end-to-end and mixed with harness overhead, so the benefit upper bound of an RVV decode kernel is not numerically quantified.

review_items.description: On the benchmark host record `cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep isa` and `vlenb` (or `riscv_hwprobe`), and confirm the DSO attribute matches the running core.
Re-run perf stat with an explicit small event set and verify counters are non-saturating (or use rdcycle-based timing) to obtain a trustworthy IPC for the decode loop.
Re-profile the isolated QT_4bit decode (e.g., perf record -e cpu-clock -c ~1000 with precise_ip) to collect hundreds of samples in decode_vector.
Add a microbenchmark that times decode_vector alone over d sizes and reports cycles per element for the current scalar path and the candidate RVV variant.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Only 3 cpu-clock samples were captured for this function, 100% on the final fsw; perf skid and a tiny sample count mean instruction-level attribution (store vs adjacent FP op) is imprecise. This does not change the root cause: the loop is the entire function body and the interval is provably scalar.

The sq-decode benchmark aggregates many qtypes (4bit/6bit/8bit/bf16/fp16) and 20 iterations each; only ~1.28ms of the 266.9ms run is attributed to benchmark_QT_4bit. The annotated function may therefore be a minor share of overall testcase wall time, which bounds the workload-level benefit estimate without changing the function-internal root cause.
Memory-bound explanation refuted: L1_dcache_load_miss_rate 0.48%, LLC_load_miss_rate 5.24%, branch_miss_rate 0.63%; the decode working set fits in L1. Slowness is not memory-latency dominated.

findings.conclusion: faiss::scalar_quantizer::QuantizerTemplate<Codec4bit<RISCV_RVV>, NON_UNIFORM, NONE>::decode_vector executes an entirely scalar per-component decode loop (0x7ac4a8-0x7ac4e8): packed 4-bit nibble unpack (srli/lbu/andi/sraw/andi 15), fcvt.s.w, fadd.s +0.5f, fdiv.s /15.0f, vmin/vdiff scalar loads, fmadd.s, fsw; 100% of the function's profile samples land in this loop and the interval contains zero v* instructions. No RVV decode kernel exists: sq-rvv.cpp defines Codec4bit/QuantizerTemplate<*,NON_UNIFORM,RISCV_RVV> as opaque markers that inherit the scalar NONE base and never override decode_vector (only DCTemplate distance-computers get RVV fast paths), so the runtime-dispatched QT_4bit path (sq-dispatch.h select) executes scalar code and the compiler did not autovectorize the packed-nibble arithmetic.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Samples are dominated by FP arithmetic (fcvt/fadd/fdiv/fmadd) and vmin/vdiff table loads, not data movement/register reordering/packing; the nibble shift/mask is only the input stage and does not dominate.
No accumulator, zero-point, or INT32 requantization contract; every lane is independent and written directly to the output.
The fp conversion is one step of the chain; the dominant signal is the contiguous affine arithmetic plus loads/stores, not conversion semantics.
code, vmin, vdiff and output are all contiguous unit-stride arrays; there is no indexed/data-dependent gather.

findings.reasoning: Disassembly shows the entire function is the loop; the readelf/mnesia metadata shows the libfaiss.so build ISA contains v1p0/zvl128b yet the hot interval has no 'v' instructions. Source cross-check (quantizers.h NON_UNIFORM NONE decode_vector contract = vmin[i]+vdiff[i]*((nibble+0.5)/15), codecs.h Codec4bit decode_component) matches the disassembly register map (vmin at 16(a0), vdiff at 24(a0), fa1/fa2 = 0.5f/15.0f). sq-rvv.cpp proves RVV Quantizer/Codec are tag types inheriting the scalar NONE base, so decode_vector cannot be RVV today; sq-dispatch.h proves QT_4bit routes to this template with SL=RISCV_RVV. Loop working set (64B code + 1KB tables) fits L1 (0.48% L1 miss), so this is compute/instruction-throughput bound, not memory bound.

alternative_explanations.explanation: On an out-of-order core, independent iterations could hide the fdiv latency via ILP, making this factor milder; severity is microarchitecture-dependent. The missing vector kernel remains the primary lever.

findings.conclusion: Within the scalar decode loop, each output serializes a dependent FP chain of fcvt.s.w -> fadd.s (+0.5f) -> fdiv.s (/15.0f, the loop-invariant constant divisor is re-divided every component) -> fmadd.s (vdiff[i]*xi+vmin[i]) plus byte-index recomputation (srli/add per iteration); GCC neither hoisted a reciprocal nor applied any wider transformation. On an in-order or low-IPC core this long-latency FP dependency and the per-element division dominate element throughput and amplify the cost of the missing vector path.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The per-component fdiv by the loop-invariant 15.0f is plain scalar code generation of a legitimate constant division; folding it to a reciprocal is a rounding/antibiotic-fp decision best made inside the vectorized elementwise kernel, not a codegen semantic-lowering defect.

findings.reasoning: The annotate shows a single fdiv.s per component inside the loop with the divisor fa2=15.0f held constant across iterations; the short FP dependency chain to the fsw is visible (7ac4c0->7ac4cc->7ac4dc->7ac4e0->7ac4e4). perf stat reports IPC=1 (unverifiable due to counter overflow, see gaps) and branch_miss 0.63%, consistent with latency/instruction-throughput-limited scalar execution rather than branch or cache stalls.

asm.reason: No hand-written .S; target code is compiler-generated scalar template code. FAISS RVV scalar-quantizer support is intrinsic/C++ (riscv_vector.h) markers in sq-rvv.cpp, not assembly. No independent .S policy/existence signal for SQ decode.

codegen.reason: Existing kernel/fallback/dispatch signal evidenced: sq-dispatch.h runtime-selects QuantizerTemplate<Codec4bit<SL>,NON_UNIFORM,SL> and at RISCV_RVV the specializations are scalar inheritances of the NONE base. Compiler generated a scalar loop including a per-component constant fdiv.s (÷15.0f). Requires codegen row scan for dispatch/semantic-lowering matches.

crypto.reason: No cryptographic primitive, cipher, hash, checksum, or GF(2^k) arithmetic in the decode loop; it is nibble unpack + FP arithmetic.

offload.reason: No matrix-engine or packed-SIMD offload opportunity in decode_vector; RVV DCTemplate distance-computation kernels already exist separately in sq-rvv.cpp and are not on this path.

operator_rvv.reason: Primary class: hot main loop (100% of samples) is a compiler-generated scalar elementwise decode (out[i]=vmin[i]+vdiff[i]*(nibble/15)) on an RVV-capable build (build ISA v1p0/zvl128b) with zero v* instructions. Lane-independent per-component contract; matches unvectorized scalar operator-loop routing.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, CSR, privilege-boundary, or runtime context-management code in the hotspot; a pure in-userspace decode loop.

string_memory.reason: Not a copy/fill/compare/checksum/scan kernel. Although codes are bit-packed (4-bit), the loop is compute-bound FP/int arithmetic (fcvt/fadd/fdiv/fmadd + table loads); L1 miss rate 0.48%, LLC 5.2% - not memory dominated. String/memory class signals do not dominate samples.

vectorized_tuning.reason: Annotated output contains zero v* instructions (entirely scalar); the class requires existing compiler/irintrinsic RVV code limited by vsetvli/bookkeeping.
